we're hiring software engineers.
 



 we're Versaunt (versatile \+ savant). Versaunt.com is the company and research lab behind Trygaas.com, the product we're building.
 



  





 Trygaas is building autonomous, self\-learning AI agents that create, run, and optimize advertising for businesses across Meta, Google, TikTok, Amazon, and eventually every major advertising platform.
 



 we just closed our pre\-seed. now we're deploying it to build the team that helps us scale.
 



  





 we don't hire often. so this is a rare one.
 



 you'd be joining our founding team and working directly with me, Keylem Collier, my cofounder and CTO Greg Steckel, and our founding engineer.
 



  





 no layers, no bureaucracy. you ship it, it's live, customers feel it the same day.
 



  





 what you'd be building
 



 the biggest problem we're trying to solve is agent behavior.
 



 how do you build an agent that does what you want it to do without having to explicitly tell it what to do every single time?
 



 how do you get an LLM to make good decisions when the answer isn't deterministic?
 



 how does an agent learn from what happened yesterday and make a better decision tomorrow?
 



 how do you give it memory, tools, context, goals, and feedback and get it to actually use all of that intelligently?
 



 how do you make an agent run for a long time, make hundreds of decisions, recover when it's wrong, and continuously get better?
 



  





 that's the type of stuff we're thinking about every day.
 



  





 we're working on autonomous agents, self\-learning agents, recursive learning, agent memory, long\-horizon tasks, evaluations, tool use, planning, and figuring out how to actually control the behavior of these systems.
 



  





 we don't need someone who just knows how to call an LLM API.
 



 we want someone who understands how these models think. someone who can look at an agent doing something stupid, figure out why it's doing it, and then figure out how to change the system so it behaves differently.
 



  





 a lot of that is going to be experimentation. a lot of it is going to be research. and a lot of it is going to be really good engineering.
 



  





 the codebase itself is big and fast\-moving. most of it is backend. a lot of it is AI.
 



 we're orchestrating autonomous agents, wiring up video and image generation models, building deep integrations across Meta, Google, TikTok, Amazon, and other platforms, and building the infrastructure that lets all of these systems work together.
 



 the hard part isn't any single piece. it's the connections.
 



  





 there's a web of agents, backend logic, models, tools, APIs, databases, and relationships running across the whole system, and you have to be able to hold it in your head, reason about it, and make smart architectural calls under pressure.
 



  





 this is systems thinking, top to bottom. critical thinking. thoughtfulness. being proactive instead of waiting to be told what to do.
 



  





 you'll mostly live in the backend, but you have to be able to move across the stack and own frontend when the work calls for it.
 



  





 the stack
 


* Python
* TypeScript
* Supabase
* Google Cloud
* AWS
* a lot of AI: agent orchestration, LLMs, video gen, image gen, platform APIs



  





 Python is probably the most important language for this role.
 



 we use a mix of Google Cloud, AWS, and Supabase. you don't need to be an expert in all three, but you should have real experience building production systems on at least one of them.
 



  





 who we want
 



 someone hungry. incredibly motivated, incredibly passionate, and looking for a startup to throw themselves into.
 



  





 more importantly, we want someone who's already proven they understand what working at a startup actually feels like.
 



  





 we're looking for people who've worked at startups before. ideally early\-stage startups where things were moving quickly, the codebase wasn't perfect, priorities changed constantly, and you still had to ship good work.
 



  





 we especially want to hear from:
 


* former founders, including the ones whose startups didn't make it. if you built something and it failed, you learned things we want on this team.
* former startup CTOs and technical founders who've already lived in the deep end
* early engineers at startups who have had real ownership over important systems
* engineers who've built autonomous agents or serious agentic systems
* people who've spent way too much time thinking about agent behavior, memory, reasoning, evaluations, self\-learning, or recursive learning
* engineers with strong system design or system architecture experience
* people who've shipped their own apps or products
* people who've interned or worked at really strong engineering organizations and learned what good production code actually looks like



  





 what matters more than years on a resume is whether you can think.
 



  





 we want people who can write really good code.
 



 code that's readable. code that's maintainable. code that's scalable. code that doesn't fall apart six months later when ten other systems depend on it.
 



  





 we use AI to code every day. you probably should too.
 



  





 but we don't want vibe coders.
 



  





 if you can't understand the code you're shipping, reason about the architecture around it, debug it when it breaks, or know when the model gave you a bad answer, this probably isn't the place for you.
 



 important context
 



  





 this is going to be hard. 50\-60 hour weeks are the norm here. everyone on the team is already working them.
 



  





 we move fast, the bar is high, and the work is demanding.
 



  





 you're going to get problems where nobody knows the answer yet.
 



 sometimes there won't be a ticket telling you exactly what to build. sometimes the problem itself won't even be clearly defined yet.
 



  





 we want people who like that.
 



 people who see a problem and start thinking about how to solve it before somebody asks them to.
 



 we want people who want the grind.
 



  





 the upside: we're a small team that's good at what we do and has a real amount of fun doing it.
 



 you'll be working out of Midtown Atlanta, mostly from the Biltmore and sometimes out of Georgia Tech, with a founding team that's building this company every day.
 



  





 the problems we're working on are some of the most interesting problems in AI right now.
 



 and for the right person, the equity could matter a lot down the line.
 



  





 logistics
 


* full time
* 100% in person in Midtown, Atlanta
* we primarily work out of the Biltmore and sometimes Georgia Tech
* this is not hybrid and not remote. if you don't live in Atlanta or aren't ready to move here, please don't apply.
* salary \+ equity \+ insurance \+ benefits
* 50\-60 hour weeks
* occasional team retreats where we travel and build together for about a week at a time. think San Francisco, New York, Chicago, Tampa.



  





 if this is you, DM me or email us founders@versaunt.com
 



  





 send us what you've built.
 



 your github. your startup. the app you shipped. the agent you built at 2am because you couldn't stop thinking about an idea. the company that failed. the weird research project nobody asked you to make.
 



 we want builders.

**Description**
 Are you passionate about applying machine learning, time series forecasting, and operations research to transform the delivery of heavy and bulky items for Amazon customers? Are you excited about working with large\-scale operational data and developing models that drive real business impact? If so, the Amazon Extra Large (AMXL) Science team may be the right fit for you.
   

  

 AMXL is Amazon's specialized business for delivering heavy and bulky items — appliances, furniture, fitness equipment, and mattresses — with a premium customer experience that includes room\-of\-choice delivery, at\-home installations, and assembly services. In this role, you will leverage large\-scale operational data to develop and deploy predictive models and optimization solutions that solve real\-world logistics and fulfillment challenges, partnering closely with scientists, engineers, and business stakeholders.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

 Apply machine learning, statistical modeling, time series analysis, and operations research techniques to build solutions for delivery routing, capacity planning, demand forecasting, workforce scheduling, and network optimization
   

  

 Analyze large\-scale historical and real\-time operational data to surface efficiency patterns, bottlenecks, and emerging trends across the AMXL network
   

  

 Develop, validate, and deploy models that improve cost\-to\-serve and customer experience
   

  

 Partner with cross\-functional teams to implement data\-driven strategies and measure impact
   

  

 Build scalable, automated pipelines for data ingestion, feature engineering, model training, and validation
   

  

 Monitor deployed model performance and communicate results through clear reporting on key operational and business metrics
   

  

 A day in the life
   

  

 You'll be part of a small, collaborative team of scientists who move fast and care deeply about the problems they solve. A typical week might involve whiteboarding a new forecasting approach with a senior scientist, partnering with engineers to push a model into production, deep\-diving into operational data to understand why a metric moved, or presenting your findings to business leaders who will act on them. The work is high\-visibility and high\-impact. The models you build will directly influence how millions of heavy and bulky items reach customers.
   

  

**About The Team**
 The AMXL Science team is a worldwide group of data scientists, applied scientists, and product managers solving Amazon's most complex heavy bulky supply chain challenges. We build forecasting models, capacity planning systems, and optimization tools that directly impact millions of customer deliveries. Our culture values scientific rigor, measurable business impact, and clear communication. We start with baselines, earn complexity, and partner closely with operations to ensure our work drives real decisions. You'll tackle problems where logistics constraints demand creative, data\-driven solutions — and see your models shape labor planning, routing, and customer experience at scale.
   

  

**Basic Qualifications**
* Master's degree in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM), or experience working in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM)
* 2\+ years of data scientist experience
* 3\+ years of data querying languages (e.g. SQL), scripting languages (e.g. Python) or statistical/mathematical software (e.g. R, SAS, Matlab, etc.) experience
* 3\+ years of machine learning/statistical modeling data analysis tools and techniques, and parameters that affect their performance experience
* 1\+ years of guiding and coaching a group of researchers experience
* 1\+ years of working with or evaluating AI systems experience
* 1\+ years of creating or contributing to mathematical textbooks, research papers, or educational content experience
* Experience applying theoretical models in an applied environment


**Preferred Qualifications**
* Ph.D. in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM)
* Knowledge of machine learning concepts and their application to reasoning and problem\-solving
* Experience in Python, Perl, or another scripting language
* Experience in a ML or data scientist role with a large technology company
* Experience in defining and creating benchmarks for assessing GenAI model performance
* Experience working on multi\-team, cross\-disciplinary projects
* Experience applying quantitative analysis to solve business problems and making data\-driven business decisions
* Experience effectively communicating complex concepts through written and verbal communication
